# Why Sukunahikona is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right

There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *sukunahikona*. This is the file on how **Sukunahikona** replaced it.

Sukunahikona's mythology in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki emphasizes that size and power are not the same.

## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Sukunahikona
- **ASCII form:** sukunahikona
- **Meaning:** "Renowned little prince"
- **Domain of influence:** Healing, Sake, Smallpox
- **Pantheon:** Japanese
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** 少彦名神
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 379 of 449

## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **少彦名神**, as Kojiki (Sukunahikona episodes) and Nihon Shoki (parallel account) record. On the evidence, it means "Renowned little prince".


Spoken, the name runs `/sɯ.kɯ.na.hi.ko.na/` — 'SOO-koo-nah-hee-koh-nah' — light, even syllables; the final vowels are soft.

## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Sukunahikona** lives at [/sukunahikona/](/sukunahikona/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sukunahikona/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sukunahikona/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sukunahikona/patterns/).

One decisive feature survives — a single, honest mark — which places the restoration in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

## Where the Name Stood First

Sukunahikona has no major independent archaeological site. His cult is preserved in shrines associated with Ōkuninushi and with healing, as well as in the textual record of the Kojiki. The temple on the web is the newest of these addresses — the first one that fits in a pocket.

## The Archetype at Work

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) seats this temple in **3 industries**, each match argued and weighted: **Food & Hospitality** (the small prince of sake; brewing is his gift.); **Healthcare, Pharma & Medicine** (the renowned little prince of healing and smallpox; folk medicine still invokes his name.); **Biotech, Longevity & Life Sciences** (healing and smallpox mastery; the small divine prince of longevity lore.). The [Resonance File](/sukunahikona/blog/resonance/) reads those seats through the myths themselves.

## In the Sacred Texts

The Japanese tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Kojiki](/texts/kojiki/) and [Nihon Shoki](/texts/nihon-shoki/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
